text:
marta: heads-up — canary bring-up for pyxis13b (int4 quant) hit memory fragmentation spikes and a couple of OOMs when requests use long completions (>512 tokens). rolling logs attached below.

devon: ouch. do you have the raw logs/trace? which config did you run — prefetch on/off, kv trim?

marta: ran with prefetch=2, kv_trim_threshold=0.2, batch_size=8, max_new_tokens default=1024. errors:
```
E 13:42:11 runtime: allocation failed: out of memory
E 13:42:11 runtime: kv_cache_alloc: requested 168MB, available 12MB
W 13:42:11 memfrag: high fragmentation ratio 0.73
```

priya: thanks. that fragmentation ratio is the smoking gun. probably lots of small allocations from int4 kernel paths + cold kv priming. quick ideas: reduce max_new_tokens default to 256 for canary, lower batch_size to 4, bump kv_trim_threshold to 0.4 and prefetch to 4 (helps amortize small allocations). also consider enabling slowstart to ramp batch concurrency.

linus: +1 on slowstart. also try disabling contiguous-pool for the model (force per-request alloc) as a temporary mitigation — less pooling can reduce fragmentation in our allocator for int4 backends.

marta: created a canary with: batch_size=4, prefetch=4, kv_trim_threshold=0.4, slowstart=true. after change, no OOMs in ~2k requests and fragmentation ratio dropped to 0.28.

perf-bot: automated summary: baseline (int4 original): p50 latency 210ms, p95 620ms, tokens/sec 140. canary (tuned): p50 230ms, p95 640ms, tokens/sec 130, OOMs 0 -> 0, memfrag 0.73 -> 0.28. cost delta +3%.

priya: nice. one more thing — evals show a small regression (~0.9 BLEU/T5-metric) on multi-turn summarization when using int4 across the board. hypothesis: quantized last layers losing precision. test: try hybrid quant (int8 last 2 layers) or use per-channel clipping.

devon: can we A/B hybrid vs full int4 on canary traffic? if quality loss is noticeable we should implement fallback to int8 for completions > 256 tokens where accuracy matters.

marta: queued an A/B with 10% traffic to hybrid-int8-last2 and 10% to int8-full for comparison. running eval harness now (summarization + instruction-following suites).

linus: if hybrid solves it, we should also add a routing rule: for routes marked as "high-quality" use hybrid by default, otherwise int4 for cost-sensitive endpoints.

priya: action items:
- set global canary defaults for pyxis13b: max_new_tokens=256, batch_size=4, prefetch=4, kv_trim_threshold=0.4, slowstart=true (marta)
- run A/B hybrid vs int4-full + int8-full and push perf+quality report (marta, devon)
- add fallback policy for "long_high_quality" requests -> int8 (linus)

marta: I'll open the PR for the defaults and link the canary results once the eval run finishes. thanks all :thumbsup:
